Hi, thank you both for your reports! I can't replicate this on sway (it's *really* aggressive at keeping the mouse captured) but I can indeed replicate the crash on weston.

The issue seems a bit complicated, as both the game and the engine are asking for a lock on the cursor, which isn't allowed even if there's an inactive lock(!) like in your case.

From the [spec](https://wayland.app/protocols/pointer-constraints-unstable-v1#zwp_pointer_constraints_v1:request:lock_pointer):
 > There may not be another pointer constraint of any kind requested or active on the surface for any of the wl_pointer objects of the seat of the passed pointer when requesting a lock. If there is, an error will be raised. See general pointer lock documentation for more details.

That seems a bit surprising and honestly somewhat unfortunate, as two separate event loops (like in this case, game and editor, or even something more trivial like app and libdecor I assume) can't easily coordinate. We can definitely implement a workaround in the embedder, it's just a bit tricky to do.

Interestingly enough confining doesn't seem to be affected by this limitation.

The pointed/confined error looks very much like #114044. Perhaps it's the same issue? Unfortunately it's somewhat known that the pointer constraint logic is a bit flimsy. It doesn't help there are weird behavior differences between compositors, which is why I haven't caught this and many other pointer issues.

BTW, @danbolt, that first crash is really interesting. Looks related to window destruction actually, and will likely require a more thorough investigation. Feel free to open a separate ticket for that :D

I asked on IRC and @zzag answered that it's a kwin bug. I also found the following (duplicate) reports:

 * https://bugs.kde.org/show_bug.cgi?id=452938 
 * https://bugs.kde.org/show_bug.cgi?id=463088

They complain about libdecor and winewayland, so we're not unique in having constraints interact with subsurfaces.

Thinking about it, we could work around locking by requesting both the child and parent surfaces, but this would be even messier to track, and confinement simply can't be worked around.

That said hopefully fixing the crash, even if constraints don't work on all compositors, will lower the severity of the issue :D

We will look into fixing kwin, but I must also say that it's probably going to take some time because we will need to make some major changes.

Regarding pointer constraints, I don't know the entire sub-surface tree structure, but maybe you could put the main contents where you need to lock the pointer in the main surface and have decoration subsurfaces below the main surface.

@zzag

> We will look into fixing kwin, but I must also say that it's probably going to take some time because we will need to make some major changes.

Yeah yeah absolutely, never intended to imply any active work on it. Sorry!

> Regarding pointer constraints, I don't know the entire sub-surface tree structure, but maybe you could put the main contents where you need to lock the pointer in the main surface and have decoration subsurfaces below the main surface.

Libdecor is not under our control (and not really relevant to kwin luckily), but in any case it and winewayland were mentioned as I didn't know before if we were the only project relying on this "implicit" protocol assumption.

The whole thing is a bit weird, as the affected subsurface is actually an "embedded" external process (a preview game instance) managed by an experimental project of mine (which will soon become a standalone library). Because of this I don't think it would even be possible to change the order of surfaces since this "embedded" surface pops in and out all the time. Still, I appreciate the tip!
Hi, can anybody give #120647 a shot? It should fix the issue.

A similar fix has been merged through #116232. Constraining will still be unreliable until #120647 is merged but now it should not crash anymore! Closing, don't hesitate to comment below if the crash still happens.
